title: The Body Has Many Uses (2)
subtitle: Body idioms for taking risks and dealing with annoying people.

idioms.mean: take a risk to help someone or say what you think
idioms.ex: Rina **stuck her neck out** and told the teacher the truth to defend me.

idioms.mean: annoy someone by always being around them
idioms.ex: My little brother keeps **getting in my hair** while I'm studying.
I'll clean my room later. Please **get off my back**!

idioms.idiom: not have a leg to stand on
idioms.mean: have no proof or good reason for what you say
idioms.ex: He says I broke the window, but he **doesn't have a leg to stand on**. There's no proof.

tip: Ganti kata ganti sesuai orangnya: *stick **my** neck out*, *get in **her** hair*, *get off **his** back*. **Get off my back** terdengar kesal, jadi pakai dengan teman, bukan dengan guru.

options: take a risk to help or speak up

meaning.q: not have a leg to stand on = ___
options: have no proof or good reason

dialogue.q: A: Mum keeps asking about my grades every hour. B: Tell her nicely to ___ for a while.
dialogue.why: Minta berhenti menekan → get off your back.

dialogue.q: A: Why are you studying in the library? B: My cousins are visiting and they keep ___.
options: having a leg to stand on
dialogue.why: Mengganggu terus → getting in my hair.

dialogue.q: A: Nobody else defended Budi in the meeting. B: I know. Only Sari ___ for him.
dialogue.why: Berani membela → stuck her neck out.

dialogue.q: A: The shop says I didn't pay, but I have the receipt! B: Then they ___.
options: don't have a leg to stand on
dialogue.why: Tidak punya bukti → don't have a leg to stand on.

correct.q: "Thanks for sticking your neck out for me in front of the boss."
"My hairdresser got in my hair, so my haircut looks great."
correct.why: Salah: get in someone's hair = mengganggu, bukan memotong rambut.

correct.q: "You have no evidence, so you don't have a leg to stand on."
"I love my coach because he always gets off my back."
correct.why: Kurang tepat: get off my back dipakai saat menyuruh orang berhenti menekan, bukan untuk memuji.

speak.q: Have you ever stuck your neck out for a friend? What happened?
speak.model: Yes, I <mark>stuck my neck out</mark> for my best friend last semester. Some classmates blamed her for a broken projector, so I told the teacher she wasn't there.
speak.label: stick one's neck out

speak.q: Who or what gets in your hair at home?
speak.model: My younger sister really <mark>gets in my hair</mark>. She always borrows my things without asking and plays loud music when I want to study.
speak.label: get in someone's hair

speak.q: When do you want people to get off your back?
speak.model: I want my parents to <mark>get off my back</mark> when they ask about my homework every five minutes. I always finish it, so they don't need to worry.
speak.label: get off someone's back

roleplay.situation: Kamu dituduh merusak laptop kelas, padahal bukan kamu pelakunya.
steps: **Student A (teman sekelas):** terus menuduh dan mengganggu (*keeps getting in my hair*).
**Student B (kamu):** minta dia berhenti menekan (*get off my back*) dan bilang dia tidak punya bukti (*you don't have a leg to stand on*).
**Student C / guru (opsional):** tanya siapa yang berani bersaksi.
**Student B:** ceritakan teman yang membela kamu (*stuck his/her neck out*).
roleplay.target: Target: percakapan 1–2 menit, semua 4 idiom terpakai. Bonus: pakai 1 idiom dari Sesi 1.
